programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see... A colored cross that divides the grid into 4 smaller grids. In the top left smaller grid you should see a shape.

The output grid size... subtract 1 from each side. 4x4 becomes 3x3

To make the output, you have to... Think of the new grid like the old grid with the divider removed. recreate the shape from the smaller top left grid of the input in the same color as the divider from the input. Mirror the shape in each of the remaining three quadrants along the x and y axis. for a total of 4 shapes in the same color. you are done.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

content.text:
The environment asked a student 6 inputs, 6 wrong, showed 1 demonstration. Student_calls_left: 0. Hmm. And "n_still_wrong": 4.

Wait, "student_calls_left": 0 — this suggests the environment did its own probing. Hmm. So it seems propose_inputs triggered the adaptive teaching. Now I have limited info.

The note: one grid (11x11) set aside: "7 objects against the example's 2". So the grid with the plus shape (D, 11x11, plus = many cells) was considered as having 7 objects vs example 2? Hmm, actually the example has 2 objects (shape + divider cross). The 11x11 grid H has diamond (8 cells) which connected forms 1 object? Plus divider -> 2 objects. Hmm. D plus shape (5 cells connected) -> 2 objects. Hmm which one is 11x11 with 7 objects? Maybe the diamond shape H: cells at (0,2),(1,1),(1,3),(2,0),(2,4),(3,1),(3,3),(4,2). Are these connected? (0,2)-(1,1) diagonal not 4-connected. So 8 cells form... let's see connectivity (4-conn): (1,1)-(2,0)? diagonal. Hmm each cell isolated? Let's check pairs: (0,2) neighbors (1,2)? not in set. So (0,2) isolated. (1,1): neighbors (0,1),(2,1),(1,0),(1,2) none in set → isolated. (1,3): neighbors (0,3),(2,3),(1,2),(1,4) none → isolated. (2,0),(2,4),(3,1),(3,3),(4,2) all isolated. So 8 isolated cells + divider = 9 objects. Hmm not 7.

Actually D plus: (2,2) center, (1,2),(3,2),(2,1),(2,3) 4-connected to center → 1 object. Divider cross → 1 object. Total 2 objects. Fine.

So the 11x11 set aside is the diamond (H) with many objects. OK.

So accepted 7. The environment asked 6, showed 1, 4 still wrong.

Hmm, student_calls_left: 0 means I can't query_student anymore? "student_calls_left" maybe refers to query_student budget. Hmm.

Wait, actually maybe propose_inputs's environment automatically runs the adaptive loop and used up all student calls. That's concerning — I have no more ability to probe.

Let me re-read the first instruction: "The environment will ask a student, holding only the pairs shown so far, to answer each one, and will show as demonstrations the ones the student gets wrong, worst first; after each, the remaining wrong answers are asked again."

So the environment did: asked 6, wrong 6, showed 1 demonstration, then re-asked remaining and 1 flipped to correct, 4 still wrong. And student_calls_left 0.

Hmm, so now what? I should probably show more demonstrations via show_transformed_input, which is separate from student calls. Then the exam.

Actually wait — maybe "student_calls_left" is the number of query_student calls I can make. Let me just try show_transformed_input to add demonstrations, which should help.

But the environment already showed 1 demonstration. Which one? Unknown. I should add more demonstrations of varied cases.

Let me show the teacher example (7x7 diag) via show_transformed_input, plus maybe a couple others with different sizes/colors. But note "nothing is shown until you call show_transformed_input".

Let me show a few: the teacher example, grid C (5x5), grid B (9x9), grid F (2x2 block). Actually more demonstrations = better, but might be redundant. Let me show 3-4.

Actually, I want the student to learn: output = 4 mirrored quadrants of TL shape, recolored to divider color, background 0, size n-1 × n-1.

Let me show:
- teacher example (7x7, diagonal, divider 7, shape 8)
- grid C (5x5, anti-diag, divider 1, shape 8)
- grid B (9x9, anti-diag, divider 4, shape 2)
- grid E (7x7, horizontal line, divider 5, shape 1)

Hmm, but I also want to be careful: showing all might be fine.

Actually the guidance says "You may also show a pair yourself with show_transformed_input." Let me show a handful.

But wait: show_transformed_input shows the pair to the Student, and also is it counted? The trial logs count show_* calls. Not a big deal.

Let me show several demos in parallel calls.

Actually careful: show_transformed_input requires the input to be accepted by verifier. My grids are accepted (7 accepted). The teacher example — is it accepted? It should be fine.

Let me do multiple show_transformed_input calls in one block. But they might depend on each other? No. However, showing too many could be wasteful but it's fine.

Hmm, but there's risk: if I show a wrong demonstration... no, show_transformed_input fills gold output, so always correct.

Let me show: teacher example, grid C, grid B, grid F. That's 4 demos covering sizes 5,7,9 and different shapes.

Actually, let me also include grid A (another 7x7) not needed.

I'll show teacher example, B, C, F, E. Let's do it.

Hmm, but maybe too many representations of the same concept is fine and increases chance student gets it.

Let me also think: is there anything tricky the student might miss? The output size n-1. The color change to divider color. The mirroring. Background 0.

One tricky bit: the shape appears in all four quadrants in output, mirrored. Also divider removed.

I think 4-5 demos suffice. Let's call.

Actually, I worry that showing the teacher example is the most important (has diagonal shape). Let me show example, C(5x5 anti-diag), B(9x9 anti-diag), F(2x2 block 9x9), E(horizontal line 7x7).

I'll batch them.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

content.text:
Now 6 demonstrations shown. Student calls left 0 so no more querying. Let's start exam.

Wait, but the "n_still_wrong: 0" in these responses suggests all previously wrong were fixed? Hmm, it shows 0 for each. Perhaps after each demonstration the environment re-asks and now 0 wrong. Good sign.

Let me do a final check: I could query_student, but calls_left=0. So just start exam.
